unresolved_questions_C: Manual requires 'sorted-cell purity/QC' for R03, but the flow cytometry in this paper controls NK-subset redistribution within the PBMC gate, not the purity of the EasySep-enriched NK fraction actually used for DNA methylation; there is no dedicated field for 'post-enrichment sort purity' distinct from 'subset distribution within PBMC' — which field (cell_context free text vs missing_data) should carry this null result, and should it be flagged NR explicitly at the sample_set level?; Whether precision_validation rows should be generated once per report/cohort (as done here, anchored to the epigenome marker family) or separately per marker_family when a report has multiple marker families in one measurement set (here: epigenome plus NK_count_or_cytotoxicity flow data) is not specified in the manual; this pilot file used one set of 7 rows anchored to the main epigenome marker family and folded the flow-cytometry null result into domain notes rather than a second full set of 7 rows.; FASLG (M-R03-003) was selected post hoc via DAVID/GO annotation rather than being named in the original genome-wide aims/methods; candidate_selection_rule vocabulary has no option cleanly describing 'single gene surfaced by post-hoc functional-annotation tool from a statistically-thresholded hit list' — used other_source_defined_rule/posthoc_or_results_only as the closest fit.; author_window_interpretation was coded redistribution_interpretation because Discussion §4.2 explicitly engages the CD56dim-redistribution hypothesis to explain the study's own null flow-cytometry result; a different reviewer might code this no_window_interpretation since the redistribution framing is used to explain an absence of effect rather than to interpret the methylation findings themselves — flagging as a genuine judgement call for comparison with B.

flagged as a tractability choice, consistent with the same granularity question raised for R42.; Untargeted metabolomics tested_universe_n is NR because the paper never states the total number of m/z features screened (only the 8 top discriminatory metabolites surviving FDR-corrected ANOVA are named in Table 3); unresolved_questions_C: cohorts.adult_stratum_separable: only mean+/-SD age (25+/-7 y) is reported for the 23 males, with no explicit inclusion-age threshold stated anywhere in Methods; recorded NR rather than inferred as all_participants_adult.; Total tested feature count (tested_universe_n) for the untargeted FIE-MS plasma metabolomics screen is not explicitly stated as a single number in the main text (only scan ranges and post-hoc discriminatory-metabolite counts are given); recorded NR in the assay-universe row (M-R12-016).; Arachidonic acid is reported as significantly elevated across all timepoints in the deficient group (Fig. 4B, narrative text) but, unlike the Table 3 metabolites, no single ANOVA F/P value for AA alone is given in the main text; charted as a reported_result_summary row without a digitized numeric effect value (effect_value_source=reported_main_text_or_table, narrative only) rather than reading the bar/line graph, per the manual's 'use numbers reported in text/tables first' rule.; marker_family vocabulary gap: salivary lactoferrin (sLac) and lysozyme (sLys) are 'recognized immune mediators' (reports.immune_link) but do not fit any specific controlled marker_family value (not mucosal_sIgA, not cytokine_or_inflammatory_mediator, not immunoglobulin_or_complement in the classic sense); charted as marker_family='other' and flagged for the team to consider adding an antimicrobial-peptide/mucosal-AMP category distinct from sIgA.; Whether the linoleic acid-arachidonic acid correlation (r=0.821, p<0.001) and the plasma-25(OH)D-to-elastase-change correlation (r=0.458, p=0.028) should be charted as separate precision_validation 'within_cohort_association' rows at the individual-measurement level (rather than folded into the marker-family-level evidence_notes as done here) is a row-granularity question flagged for team standardisation, parallel to the R42 row-unit question.

Whether whole-blood transcriptome deconvolution (CIBERSORTx) and gene-marker-based immune-cell enrichment (CellMarker 2.0) should be classified as 'immune_cell_omics'/'direct_immune_cell_or_count' for reports.immune_link and marker_family, given the authors' own caveat that these computational estimates need flow-cytometry/single-cell confirmation (p.17-18 Discussion).; author_window_interpretation classification is borderline: the paper describes transient NK/CD8+ T-cell 'mobilization' with return to baseline (classic redistribution phenotype) but never uses 'open window', 'immunosuppression', 'susceptibility' or 'redistribution' terminology – charted as no_window_interpretation; 44/175 participants completed a second, post-training acute bout (same participants, explicit timing, baseline/comparator) that structurally resembles the Support B pattern, but this report explicitly excludes that data from analysis – confirm whether a forward-linkage note (no Support B rows created here, but a second-bout dataset exists and may appear in a future MoTrPAC report) is sufficient, or whether a placeholder Support B flag should be recorded now.; measurements.omics_integration was set to 'multiple_omics_parallel' for every row (reflecting the study's parallel 3-platform design) rather than 'single_omics' (reflecting that each specific differential-abundance test is run on one platform at a time) – confirm the intended scope of this field (design-level vs analysis-level).
unresolved_questions_C: Participant-denominator discrepancy: the report gives at least three different overall-cohort numbers that are not reconciled in the accessible text — 206 'randomized before the suspension' (p.53 Statistical limitations), 176 'completed the baseline acute test' (p.20 STAR Methods), and 175 (99%) with >=1 biospecimen collected (p.20; used as Table 1's N). cohorts.n_recruited and report_cohort_links.n_analyzed were both set to UNCLEAR pending human adjudication of which denominator the manual intends as 'n_recruited' vs 'n_analyzed'.; No exact per-timepoint x per-platform x per-group participant n could be located in the main text, Table 1, Table S1/S2 (media-1.xlsx), the Key Resources Table (media-2.docx) or the supplementary figure legends (supplement-3.pdf); only platform-by-group overall N (Table S1) and a qualitative statement that subgroup n can be 'as small as 4 participants' are available. All 14 sample_sets rows therefore carry n_participants = NR at the exact-timepoint level. This is the central calibration question this report's pilot_purpose ('multi-platform different n and repeated samples') was selected to test: should sample_sets rows be created for every group x platform x timepoint combination even when n is unresolvable at that granularity (as done here), or should rows be collapsed to the platform-by-group level when per-timepoint n is unavailable?; Row-unit choice for jointly-reported immune candidates without individual statistics (e.g., M7 chemokine/interleukin group; M8 granzyme family; M9 NK receptor gene set): this pilot used one grouped named_immune_candidate row per jointly-reported set rather than one row per gene/protein, because the source gives no per-feature numeric value outside figure heatmaps that were not digitized. An alternative reading of the manual would split these into one row per named gene/protein with effect_value=NR on each. Needs adjudication.; Text reports NK-cell-marker gene 'KLRK1 (KLRC2)' (p.15), which appears to conflate two distinct HGNC gene symbols; recorded verbatim in M9 rather than corrected, and flagged rather than silently resolved.; Exact blood-transcript timepoint for the RE-unique CD44 increase (M13) is not stated in the main text; only the skeletal-muscle companion timing (3.5 h) is explicit. Linked provisionally to the RE 3.5 h sample_set (SS-R19-09) as the nearest documented timepoint — needs confirmation against Figure S8A-B, which was not digitized in this pass.; Whether a precision_validation row set should be built once per report/cohort (as done here, 7 rows) or once per measurement_id (which would require on the order of 7 x 18 = 126 rows for this report's 18 measurement rows) is not resolved by the manual text consulted; this pilot used the report/cohort-level simplification and flags it for discussion.; No formal full-text screening disposition exists for this pilot item (reports.screening_decision_reviewer_A/B and consensus_screening_decision set to NA rather than NR, since the omission is a scope choice for this charting-only task rather than a reporting gap in the source).; The companion papers repeatedly cited as 'REF, in submission/preparation' (Clinical Landscape, Multi-Omic Landscape, Skeletal Muscle companion, Adipose Tissue companion) were not retrieved; some cohort-level fields (exact eligibility criteria, exact n screened before randomization) may be resolvable only from those companion manuscripts, which are outside this pilot's provided fulltexts.; A possible linked 2026-01 bioRxiv preprint version was mentioned for a different pilot report (R01) in PILOT_README, not R19; no separate earlier/later version of R19 itself was identified beyond the 'v2, posted 2026-03-11' label on the consulted PDF — version history before v2 (e.g., a v1) was not located or retrieved in this pilot.

unresolved_questions_B: scope_stream boundary case (the report's designated pilot purpose): is a weekly cumulative training block with an ambiguous ~48h-inferred sampling delay (Figure 1 axis only, not stated in prose) enough to count as B_support_repeated_bouts (4 repeated 'bouts' = W1-W4) with baseline W0, or must it stay 'background'/'uncertain' because no single identifiable bout and no stated exercise_end_definition exist? This determines whether R42 ever reaches formal charting as A/B evidence.; Pooled discovery vs individual-level ELISA validation (the report's second designated focus): Methods 2.10 does not state whether the ELISA assay for SEMG-1/PIP/PDGFRL/NDPK (Table 7) was performed on the SAME pooled urine sample used for iTRAQ (n=1 per timepoint, in which case the mean±SD in Table 7 would need another explanation) or on individual participant aliquots (n~15). Either way it is same-cohort/same-collection-round validation, not an independent cohort -- but the manual's independent_validation_and_use domain and n_biological_samples/n_participants fields need a human decision on how to code genuinely unresolvable pooled-vs-individual ambiguity from an inaccessible-data paper.; Granularity of precision_validation: this file scores the 7 domains at marker_family level (leukocyte_redistribution, T_cell_subsets_or_function, proteome) rather than per individual named marker (e.g. SEMG-1 separately from the other 23 proteins), to keep the row count tractable; the validation-readiness map's intended unit of analysis ('per-marker') may require per-marker domain rows instead, especially for the 4 ELISA-validated proteins.; sample_role/time_bin controlled vocabulary gap: none of 'immediate_post'/'recovery_post'/'during_exercise' cleanly describes a sample taken after a week of repeated daily training blocks; 'other' or 'UNCLEAR' were the only non-guessing options used here, which may need a dedicated vocabulary value for weekly/periodic training-monitoring samples if such designs recur across the full corpus.; Whether the 24 named co-differential proteins (Tables 5-6) should be coded as 'named_immune_candidate' (post-hoc discovery, candidate_prespecification_status=posthoc_or_results_only) as done here, or whether an exploratory iTRAQ screen with a broad immune-biomarker aim effectively pre-specifies ALL annotatable proteins as candidates, changing candidate_selection_basis/candidate_prespecification_status coding guidance for untargeted omics discovery papers generally.; age_range/adult_stratum_separable confidence: only mean±SD age (19.2±0.7 y) is given, no explicit range; 'all_participants_adult' was used based on university-student context and informed-consent procedure, but this is an inference, not a stated range -- flagged as medium/low confidence.
unresolved_questions_C: Is the fixed training-week-to-Sunday-sample schedule (Fig. 1) sufficiently well-defined timing to qualify this as Support B (repeated identified bouts with known bout-to-sample timing), or does it remain background/FT04 because the 'bout' is a 5-session weekly block rather than one identified session? This is the core calibration question flagged by pilot_purpose for R42.; Methods 2.10 does not state whether the ELISA validation of SEMG1/PIP/PDGFRL/NDPK (Table 7) used pooled or individual urine; the mean+/-SD + one-way-ANOVA presentation suggests individual-level sampling, in contrast to the explicitly POOLED iTRAQ discovery samples (Methods 2.7: 'combined into one urine sample for each time point'), but this is inferred, not stated. Recorded as UNCLEAR in sample_sets.matrix/n_biological_samples for SS-R42-16..20.; Row-unit choice for Tables 5-7: each co-differential/validated protein was charted as ONE measurement row spanning all 4 weekly fold-change/concentration values (rather than 4 separate per-week-comparison rows). Manual's 'per named candidate x comparison' row unit is ambiguous for this kind of multi-timepoint table; flag for team decision on the standard convention.; cohorts.adult_stratum_separable: only mean+/-SD age (19.2+/-0.7 y) is given for the 15 male students, with no explicit inclusion age criterion or range; marked UNCLEAR rather than all_participants_adult, since the strict rule is not to infer.; Whether the GO-annotated 'immune system process' proteins (Fig. 4, 10 of the 24 co-differential proteins) should be separately tagged as the manual's 'named immune candidate' subset (aims/methods-linked), given the paper's stated aim is explicitly immune-biomarker discovery even though protein selection itself was an unbiased fold-change/co-expression screen, not an a priori immune-target list.; marker_family vocabulary: urinary immunoglobulin fragments (IGKC, IGLV3-21, IGLV4-69, IGLV2-18) and complement factor CD55 (Table 6) arguably fit 'immunoglobulin_or_complement' rather than 'proteome'; charted here as 'proteome' (omics-platform-based) for internal consistency with the other 23 iTRAQ-discovered proteins, but this is a judgment call worth standardising.

unresolved_questions_B: Blood matrix (plasma vs serum) for the Olink panel is not stated anywhere in the available main text or the two supplement sheets (Proteins, LMM_results); matrix recorded as NR across all sample_sets rows.; Exact exercise modality (cycling, treadmill, other) is not specified in the available text beyond '40-min aerobic exercise session at 60% VO2peak'; exercise_mode recorded as NR.; Article-type/publication_status classification: this is a 4-page 'Did You Know?' section item in Acta Physiologica, containing genuinely new primary data (n=12 trial) rather than a classic editorial/commentary, but the controlled vocabulary's closest non-'peer_reviewed_version_of_record' option is 'editorial_or_commentary'. Coded as peer_reviewed_version_of_record; manual could usefully add a 'short_report_or_research_letter' category.; Narrative-vs-statistics discrepancy: the main text states IFN-gamma 'falls below baseline levels already 15 min after the onset of acute exercise', but the supplement's LMM shows this timepoint is not statistically significant (adjusted p=0.369); only the 1h-post estimate is significant. Several other proteins (PDGF-B, CCL4, CCL8/IL8) are also significant at only one of six post-baseline timepoints. Manual should clarify whether measurement rows must follow strict per-timepoint statistical significance or may also reflect narrative-described directional trends.; Pilot-purpose note flags this report as sharing a cohort with another publication ('共享队列'); within this 2-report pilot batch no other report originates from the same TU Dortmund group, so cohort overlap could not be checked here and should be verified by D/A against the wider corpus (e.g., the Kurgan et al. 2025 bioRxiv preprint cited as ref. 6, from a different group, is not an overlap candidate).; Row-volume issue: a full 'every named candidate regardless of significance' extraction would require up to 92 proteins x 6 post-baseline timepoints = 552 potential measurement rows; this pilot recorded 1 assay-universe row + 6 representative named-candidate rows (comparison = the single most text-anchored timepoint per protein) rather than the full matrix. Same feasibility concern raised independently for R61.
unresolved_questions_C: Blood matrix (plasma vs serum) is never explicitly named in the accessible 4-page text; 'venous blood samples were collected... and processed immediately after collection' (p.1) does not specify the final analyte matrix for the Olink assay. Recorded as UNCLEAR in sample_sets.matrix; the manual should state whether reviewers may infer a platform's typical default matrix (Olink PEA is commonly run on plasma) or must always mark UNCLEAR absent an explicit statement.; Exercise modality (cycling vs treadmill/other ergometer) is likewise never explicitly named; only '40-min aerobic exercise session at 60% of their VO2peak' is given (p.1), and the Figure 1A icon is not machine-readable text. Recorded sample_sets.exercise_mode as UNCLEAR.; Shared-cohort question (this report's own pilot_purpose explicitly names this as the calibration target): reference 6 (Kurgan et al. 2025 bioRxiv, 'Body Fluid Proteomic Landscape of Acute Exercise') and this report share the same TU Dortmund Sports Medicine research context and a similarly named online data portal, but authors do not overlap and the text does not state whether participants/cohorts overlap. The manual does not specify how much circumstantial similarity (institution, topic, dashboard naming) should trigger a mandatory cross-report cohort-identity check versus being left to study_notes as a flag for human adjudication.; Row-volume policy for large targeted-panel omics (92 quantified Olink proteins, 737-row full LMM supplement table): this pilot created 1 assay-universe row + 44 named-candidate rows (one per significant protein, using the single strongest of up to 6 timepoint-level LMM coefficients per protein) rather than fully enumerating all 92 proteins x 7 timepoints (=644 potential rows) or all 48 non-significant proteins individually. The manual should state explicitly whether full timepoint-level enumeration is required for dense repeated-measures kinetic designs, or whether a 'strongest timepoint' summary per named candidate (as done here) is an acceptable extraction unit.; marker_family assignment required subjective judgement for several Olink Immuno-Oncology analytes that are not classic leukocyte/cytokine markers (e.g. growth factors FGF2, PDGF-B, EGF, VEGFA, VEGFR-2, ANGPT2; tumour marker CAIX; costimulatory receptors CD40/CD40-L/TWEAK/TNFSF14); these were coded 'other' by default, which is defensible but not rule-driven, and may understate immune-specific family counts in downstream figures.; This report's publication format is a 4-page Wiley 'Did You Know?' short communication/research letter without separate headed Methods/Results/Discussion sections, an explicit ethics-approval number, or some standard methodological details (see above). The manual does not currently distinguish full-length original articles from short-communication formats for completeness expectations; flagging this format difference as a possible source of systematic NR/UNCLEAR rates across pilot reports.; reports.version_date / version_label: no explicit online-first date distinct from the Accepted date (14 Oct 2025) and issue pagination (e70125) is given in the text.

unresolved_questions_B: Study unit structure: Study 1 (field marathon) and Study 2 (lab crossover) were modelled as two separate study_families/cohorts under one report, since they have different participants, settings and designs; the manual's examples do not explicitly cover a single report with two unrelated sub-studies of this kind, so this structural choice should be confirmed with A/D.; sample_sets.time_bin for Study 1 post-marathon sample: the text gives only 'immediately after the marathon' with clock-times (3:11 PM +-48 min) and no numeric minutes-since-finish; 0_to_lt30min was assigned by interpreting 'immediately' as consistent with other exercise-immunology usage, but this is an inference, not a reported number - flag for calibration of how the manual wants 'immediately after' handled when no numeric offset is given.; Supplementary Table S2 (Study 2) merged-cell parsing: the python-docx extraction of the Men/Women columns produced an inconsistent number of data columns (likely a merged-cell artefact in the original Word table), so sex-stratified EX/CON values could not be confidently extracted; only 'All' values were used in measurement rows.
